data.title: The Collapse of Western Rome
sentences: The fall of the Western Roman Empire was not a single event, but a slow dissolution centuries in the making.
Following the instability of the third century, Diocletian attempted to stabilize the state by dividing the empire into East and West.
However, economic decay, hyperinflation, and a reliance on foreign mercenaries left the Western borders fragile.
The arrival of the Huns in Europe triggered a mass migration of Germanic tribes across Roman frontiers.
After the devastating defeat at Adrianople in 378 AD, the myth of Roman invincibility was shattered forever.
By 410 AD, the city of Rome fell to the Visigoths, marking the first time in eight centuries that the capital had been sacked.
The loss of North Africa to the Vandals crippled Rome's grain supply and tax revenue.
Finally, in 476 AD, the Germanic leader Odoacer deposed the teenage emperor Romulus Augustulus.
By sending the imperial regalia to Constantinople, Odoacer ended the Western line, while the East survived as the Byzantine Empire.
